clue.text: Thomas the poet located, oddly, in Germany

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters of the country name

explanation.surface: A biographical note placing a poet called Thomas in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard; the clue gives his first name so the answer is his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray is the surname of the eighteenth-century English poet whose first name was Thomas.

clue.text: Asti and rum I mixed for Italian treat

indicators.note: drinks that are mixed are stirred together, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of Asti, rum and I, leaving out the joining word

explanation.surface: A cocktail of Italian sparkling wine and rum, mixed up as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the fodder words and adds no letters. Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is a well-known Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.

clue.text: For each boy accomplished looking good

blocks.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a son is a boy child
able means skilled or accomplished

explanation.surface: A description of an accomplished boy who also happens to look good.
explanation.definitionFit: Personable means pleasant in appearance and manner, so attractive or good-looking.

clue.text: Appreciation of taste that artist finds helpful, we hear

blocks.note: a palette is the board an artist mixes paints on

explanation.surface: An artist praised for finding good taste helpful in their work.
explanation.walkthrough: The painter's board and the roof of the mouth are pronounced the same but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A palate is the sense of taste, and figuratively a person's ability to appreciate flavours.

clue.text: Tolerate Conservative act that's inviting for consumer

blocks.note: to bear is to tolerate or put up with
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A political note about a Tory statute that might tempt shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests consumer legislation, but the consumer is someone eating: a bear claw is a sweet pastry shaped like a paw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear claw is an American sweet pastry, something tempting for whoever is going to eat it.

clue.text: Blasted noblewomen ignoring negative sign, first and last

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving something out, so some letters are dropped from the long word
first and last say where the two removals happen: one at the start, the other at the end

blocks.note: taken as written; that the kept letters also run inside it is a coincidence of the two removals, not a hidden word
no is a negative answer; it comes off the front
an omen is a sign of things to come; it comes off the end

explanation.surface: Aristocratic ladies are cursed at for disregarding a negative signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first and last' places the two removals: the negative from the start and the sign from the end, leaving the middle four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blew is the past tense of blow, as a gale or explosion blasted, so the two verbs match in tense.

clue.text: Eco echoed as novelist

indicators.note: an echo repeats a sound, so the word is identified by how it is said

blocks.note: eco is a prefix meaning environmentally friendly, which is green

explanation.surface: Umberto Eco being repeated, or copied, as a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Eco looks like the Italian novelist, but here it means green in the environmental sense; Graham Greene wrote Brighton Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was a twentieth-century English writer of novels such as The Power and the Glory.

clue.text: Scanned money, top-sliced 80% of cash

indicators.note: slicing off the top of a down answer removes its first letter

surface padding that confirms the step: four of the five letters of the slang word survive

explanation.walkthrough: '80% of cash' confirms the step: four of the five letters of the slang word for cash remain once the first goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan a text is to look over it, so scanned is a past-tense synonym of read.

clue.text: State again backed e-bank charge

a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A complaint restated about a charge levied by an online bank.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the e-bank part goes backwards; the charge follows it as written.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say something once more, repeating a statement already made.

clue.text: Stout or beer that's taken right to heart

to heart means moved into the middle of the remaining letters

blocks.note: lager is a type of beer
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A pub choice between stout and a beer that someone has grown fond of.
explanation.walkthrough: The beer's final R is lifted out and set into the centre, so the same five letters are rearranged. Stout looks like the drink, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout as an adjective means fat or heavily built, which is large.

clue.text: Keats and this other poet share food after initial disagreement

blocks.note: surface padding naming the poet whose name differs only at the start

eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Two poets sharing a meal after an early quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats and the answer both end in the same four letters meaning food; only their first letters differ. W. B. Yeats was an Irish poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeats is the Irish poet, a second writer of verse beside the Keats named in the clue.

clue.text: Leaderless school acquiring principal that points the way

blocks.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school without a leader taking on a principal who will show the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a well-known boarding school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrowhead is the pointed tip of an arrow, or an arrow-shaped sign indicating direction.

clue.text: School subject that is included in the Carolinas, along with English

blocks.note: SC and NC are the postal abbreviations for South and North Carolina

explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is the usual crossword route to ie; it slots between the two state codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Science is a subject taught in schools, covering physics, chemistry and biology.

clue.text: Lose little time in scattering petals or other part of flower

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so one letter is dropped
scattering spreads things about, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to scatter petals quickly, or some other floral part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little time' is the single letter abbreviation, removed before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepal is one of the leaf-like parts outside the petals that protects a flower bud.

clue.text: Their arms point forwards for this dance

definitions.text: Their arms point forwards for this dance

blocks.note: surface reading: dancers stretching their arms out in front
setter's reading: cavalry soldiers whose arms, their weapons, are long spears held pointing ahead, give their name to a quadrille

explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' means weapons, not limbs: the soldiers carry lances couched forward. The same word names a nineteenth-century square dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancers is a quadrille, a set dance for four couples, named after cavalry soldiers armed with lances.

clue.text: They carry papers as a convenience, following directions

blocks.note: the four compass points north, east, west and south
agents act on someone else's behalf, for their convenience

explanation.surface: Couriers who carry documents as a favour, doing as they are told.
explanation.walkthrough: Newsagents are also convenience shops, which gives the middle phrase a second fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsagents are shopkeepers who stock and sell newspapers and magazines.

clue.text: Produce clippings easy to look through in hearing

blocks.note: sheer fabric is fine enough to see through

explanation.surface: Clippings that are easy to read through while listening.
explanation.walkthrough: The sheep farmer's verb and the see-through adjective are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To shear is to cut wool or hair, producing clippings or fleece.

clue.text: What sounds like desirable job description? Exactly

indicators.note: sounds like tells you to match the pronunciation and change the spelling

blocks.note: a desirable job is called a plum job, so plum is its description

explanation.surface: A question about how to describe a desirable job, answered with a firm agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumb as an adverb means precisely, as in plumb in the centre, from a weight hanging straight.

clue.text: Fashion shade announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so its sound is what counts

blocks.note: a hue is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A fashion house declaring the colour of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Fashion looks like the clothing industry, but it is the verb meaning to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to shape by cutting, as in fashioning a figure out of stone or timber.

clue.text: Trainer may use it for transporting gym equipment before fight

definitions.text: Trainer may use it for transporting

blocks.note: a vaulting horse is gymnastic apparatus
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A personal trainer carrying gym equipment to a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: The trainer is a racehorse trainer, not a fitness coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A horsebox is a vehicle or trailer that racehorse handlers use to move their animals.

clue.text: Complaint one enters when maltreated

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who has been treated badly lodges a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A whine is a feeble, persistent grumble, a kind of complaint.

clue.text: Scheme to raise a lot of interest

definitions.text: to raise a lot of interest

blocks.note: first meaning: a secret plot

blocks.clueFragment: to raise a lot of interest
blocks.note: second meaning: to fascinate or arouse curiosity

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about money earning interest; the second meaning is curiosity, not finance.

clue.text: On part of journey, superficially damage trunks, say

explanation.definitionFit: Swimming trunks are shorts, an example of clothing worn on the legs.

clue.text: Improved on try for top award in audition

blocks.note: gold is the top medal awarded in a competition

clue.text: Gossip about crazy guy in Tea Party

the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Rumours about an unhinged member of the American Tea Party movement.

clue.text: Person making fatal choices botched clue about left, right?

clue.text: Answer's found in part of recipe that contains multiple steps

clue.text: Frequent bar in light opera

clue.text: With another club, possibly, beat uncovered backside
